concepts.def: Probability of harm = Hazard x Vulnerability x Exposure / Capacity.
Susceptibility; poverty, age, gender, governance shape it.

walkthroughs.body_html: UNDRR (2009) defines risk as a function of hazard, exposure and vulnerability divided by capacity. Two areas may face the same hazard but differ in risk: Japan and Haiti both face M7+ earthquakes but vulnerability differs vastly due to building codes and GDP.

Wisner et al's Pressure and Release model traces vulnerability to root causes (limited resources, ideologies), dynamic pressures (rapid urbanisation, environmental degradation), and unsafe conditions (fragile housing, dangerous locations). Applied to Hurricane Katrina shows social structure of disaster.

Haiti Mw 7.0 (12 January) killed 220000. Chile Mw 8.8 (27 February, 500x more energy) killed 525. Differences: Chile GDP per capita 9x Haiti's; strict building codes since 1985; functioning emergency services. Demonstrates that magnitude alone does not determine risk.
